newsitem.title: UK: SHELL IN CO-OPERATION TALKS WITH UK SUPERMARKETS.
newsitem.headline: SHELL IN CO-OPERATION TALKS WITH UK SUPERMARKETS.

text.p: Royal Dutch/Shell Group said it is in talks with one or two British supermarket chains to join forces to fight intense competition in the UK petrol market.
The Anglo-Dutch oil giant already struck a deal in the Netherlands with the country's largest retailer Koninklijke Ahold to have food shops at Shell's petrol stations.
But Shell declined to name the chains it is in talks with in Britain. Chairman John Jennings said there was nothing "substantial" to announce at this stage.

But ventures with supermarkets were "an area where we want to learn fast," Jennings said, adding they could be powerful weapons to fight rivals in de-regulated markets such as Britain and Japan. Ferocious competition in the British petrol market stems for a large part from retailers selling fuels at discount prices at their supermarkets.
Jennings said marketing margins in Britain had recovered "somewhat", but said they could still not be considered satisfactory.
British Petroleum , which has already struck a "food and fuels" co-operation deal with retailer Safeway , said on Tuesday that the UK petrol price war had cost it $140 million last year.
Shell said it had not quantified the impact.
